regions.merged_text: Yes, just starting my 77th anniversary as your wrie held me up at my above, first period after the date, - just starting to answer your charitable letter received this am. Many thanks for your generosity as well as for so kind a rememberence on this ocasion. I had some friends down from Detroit yesterday to remind me of and to congratulate on my 76thB-day. I was on retreat last week and on Sunday went to Detroit and in the evening to Windsor, Ontario, Can. to the "Send-off celebration" given to Fr. Julius O.F.M.Cap. by his old friends in the parish of his childhood - Our Lady of Prompt Succor. He was supposed to leave for Guam Missions in November. It was Monday evening when we returned and I felt I must get at my work and catch up, etc. Well, Deo gratia for every thing! Thanks be to Go. As to your German candidate farm-manager's system of religion - lutheran: well, it might be better and would certainly be more promising if he were Imown to be a practical Catholic; but if he give evidence of honesty and the fear of God and thrift as best he can - with experience bhind him, I would be water inclined to him rather than to a fresh graduate from most/ of our universities who have had little or no practical farm experien. After all the lutherans, as a rule, know more of Christianity than most any of the other non-catholic Christian denominations. Besides, these day protestantism as a whole seems to be rapidly crumbling. The whole trouble with honest protestants - and thank God there a lot of such - is that thy simply do not know the real relationship between their own denomination and the Mother-church. Otherwise equal, I would take a conscientious lutheran ten times in preference to just a nominal Catholic. I know from childhood how to appreciate German lutherans. If the change of clamate benot too radical and this man's wife and daughter can aide, etc, I would be inclined in his favor. In the mean time, however, let us pray for divine grudance - especially turning to St. Josep and the Poor Souls. How about inviting the latter to - especially our own relatives amongst them - to take an interest with us and become missionaries with a promise to enroll them, e.g., for a certain % of the proffits. That I always call a double charity; to our neighbor, viz, to our fellow members of the militent Church, the missionaries and their work and then to the Church-suffering, the poor, holy souls.
